issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all accessor/mutator methods use camelCase names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents) as specified in the UML and expected by the problem. This naming mismatch makes the solution code inconsistent and uncompilable, and conflicts with the attribute names students are expected to add according to the problem statement and template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names in the solution consistent with the UML and with the constructor/getter/setter usage. Rename the declared fields to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (or update all constructor and method references to match the declared names). Ensure field names, constructor parameters and all method references use the same identifiers so the code compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the expected API use camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). In the provided solution Lecture.java the attributes are declared using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor, getters/setters and methods use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual attributes across artifacts (and even within the solution file) creates mapping confusion for students and can cause compilation errors or wasted time locating the correct fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent naming convention for the attributes across all artifacts. Rename the declared fields in the solution to the camelCase names used in the UML and methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively change all uses to match the snake_case declarations. Prefer matching the problem statement's camelCase to avoid student confusion and to follow Java conventions; update constructor and methods to reference the declared fields.
